<!-- pr-reviewer: 2e7f788568aad628017eee054aaec293bfe0c905 -->

Needs changes before merge - one pin (the trace's downstream refusal is explicit but not pinned).

Reviewed the head 2e7f78856 of side/path-kernel (base 25f3838db, 1 commit, merged clean - no conflicts, already up to date). Comments on the requested focus of this PR: the new medial-axis code and the trace chain region.

What looks good
- Provenance on every new file (geometry `delaunay.rs`, `medial.rs`, `side_offset.rs`; pathkernel `region_chain.rs`, `choice.rs`, `lead.rs`, `medial.rs`, `trace.rs`, `helix.rs`, `all.rs`). Published sources only (Blum 1967; Brandt & Algazi 1992; Bowyer/Watson 1981; Devillers et al. 2002; Foskey et al. 2003 / Attali & Montanvert 1996; Tiller & Hanson 1984; Choi & Park 1999; Ramer 1972 / Douglas & Peucker 1973; Held 1991; our own design records). Not a port of the old spines.
- Degenerate input refused by name, never crashed or hung: non-positive/NaN tolerance or angle refused (`medial.rs`), empty region refused, >200,000 boundary samples refused, Delaunay returns Ok([]) for <3 points and errors on non-finite points (never panics), side_offset refuses <2 points, non-finite points or distance, zero distance and a no-length path, `Chain::closed`/`Chain::open`/`Selection` validation refuses empty/collinear/crossing chains, and a neck-touching area is pinned to produce an axis without crash (`geo2d::medial::tests`).
- The new medial axis is sorted by point set (input order and start vertex never affect it - pinned in geometry and pathkernel), theta-pruned, RDP-simplified, and spur-count is named in a note.
- Follow-up #4236: the record (decision 4, `docs/decisions/4176-kernel-guides-medial-trace-helix.md`) names the exact ordering - the entry stage refuses a chain region (`NOT_PLANAR`, `entry/room.rs:28-29`), the law kit reads the tool from `planar()` (`tests/laws/kit.rs:169-178`), so a trace cannot run through all stages yet - and #4236 exists to cover it.

Results (local, this worktree; runner not applicable - side-branch base). Independent confirmation on the touched crates (per the author's gate: batch 1223 steps, 0 failed, 88.9 min; light 7/7, both on 2e7f78856, trusted as reported - not re-run):
- `cargo test -p camcraft-geometry --lib`: 94 passed (incl. medial, delaunay, side_offset)
- `cargo test -p camcraft-pathkernel --test laws`: 134 passed (incl. guide_medial, guide_trace, guide_helix, guide_laws)
- `cargo test -p camcraft-pathkernel --lib`: 4 passed
- `cargo test -p camcraft-motion --test pass_start_levels kernel_`: 22 passed (incl. kernel_guides: trace, medial, circle rings, helix against the #4153 goldens)
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-geometry -p camcraft-pathkernel -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean

Targeted tests: example catalog untouched by this diff (no post/toolpath change). The full heavy lanes are not run for a P2 PR under the safety floor (no `P1`); the light lane is taken as the author's 7/7 on this head, not re-run.

Requested before merge
1. Pin the trace chain region's downstream refusal. The entry stage refuses a non-planar region by name (`NOT_PLANAR`, `crates/pathkernel/src/entry/stage.rs:25` via `entry/room.rs:29`) and the law kit reads the tool from `planar()` (`crates/pathkernel/tests/laws/kit.rs:170`), but no test pins either refusal on a chain region: a silent behavior change (entry begins to accept a chain region, or the kit starts to accept one, without the follow-up being updated) would pass. Add one test, e.g. in `crates/pathkernel/tests/laws/guide_trace.rs` (next to `each_refusal_of_the_trace_is_named`), asserting `EntryStage` refuses a chain region with `NOT_PLANAR`. Small addition; do not change the downstream code.

Questions / notes (not blocking)
- The medial planner guards a sample cap (`MEDIAL_TOO_FINE`) but the geometry layer's own cap is a backstop; both fire, naming their reason. Good.
- The trace L1-L4 law checks are read on the guide and the stand-in order stage (`guide_trace.rs`), because the kit's stages plan an area. That is the documented ordering (decision 4), not a shortcut.
- The new `medial_tests.rs` and `kernel_guides.rs` join the geometry lib suite and the `pass_start_levels` directory suite - good placement.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

<!-- pr-reviewer: ebc9663503f6dd87947ac6d5d5b0d6ced44ef08d -->

Ready for the maintainer to merge - the one finding of the last review (the trace chain region's downstream refusal was unpinned) is fixed and verified on this head.

Reviewed the head ebc966350 of side/path-kernel (base 25f3838db, unchanged since the last review; trial merge clean - the base is an ancestor of the head, no conflicts). This is a re-review of the one-commit fix on 2e7f78856: the diff 2e7f78856..ebc966350 is only `crates/pathkernel/tests/laws/guide_trace.rs` (+59 lines). No stage logic changed.

What looks good
- The fix is one table test, `guide_trace::each_later_stage_refuses_the_chain_region_of_a_trace_by_name`, and it is one test for the whole class (every later stage that reads the region refuses by its named reason), not a per-stage patch.
- The test pins the right stages and the right reasons. Every stage on this branch that reads a kernel region: `EntryStage::entry` and `EntryStage::exit` (real code, refusing `entry::NOT_PLANAR` via `entry/room.rs:29` and `entry/exit.rs:111`), the law kit `planar` (`tests/laws/kit.rs:169` - `kit::NOT_PLANAR`) and the law kit `run` (same refusal at its region read, `kit.rs:178`). The order, load and link stages have only a trait on this branch (no planner; `load.rs`, `link.rs`, `order.rs`), so nothing to pin there - that is #4236.
- The test fails loudly. It runs every leg inside `catch_unwind`: a panic is a failure of that leg, an accepted plan is a failure (`accepts the chain region of a trace`), and a refusal is matched against the expected reason string. It does not assert a pass.
- The decision file `docs/decisions/4176-kernel-guides-medial-trace-helix.md` is accurate on this head: decision 4 names the entry stage's `NOT_PLANAR` refusal and the kit's `planar()` tool-read, and the guide choices moved to `guide/choice.rs` with the same public paths by re-export (`guide.rs` is 255 lines, under the ~400-line rule). No AIR-constant issue in this PR's files (that is a different PR, #4234).

Results (local, this worktree .claude/worktrees/cc-pr4244-review, sccache, CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=6 CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS=6)
- `cargo test -p camcraft-geometry --lib`: 94 passed (medial, delaunay, side_offset)
- `cargo test -p camcraft-pathkernel --test laws`: 135 passed (incl. guide_trace, guide_medial, guide_helix, guide_laws; the new test runs by name: `1 passed`)
- `cargo test -p camcraft-pathkernel --lib`: 4 passed
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-geometry -p camcraft-pathkernel --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean
- The full batch was green on 2e7f78856 (1223 steps, 0 failed, 88.9 min) per the author's report and the previous review; the new head adds one test file, so it is not re-run here. The light lane (7 steps, 0 failed) was green on 2e7f78856 per the same report; not re-run for the same reason.

Targeted tests
- No post or toolpath change - the example catalog is not run.
- The new test is the pinning test for this finding - run by name (1 passed).
- P2 PR, no heavy step is owed (not P1).

Requested before merge
- Nothing.

Questions / notes (not blocking)
- The `kit::run` leg refuses at its region read, so the stand-in order, load, link and entry planners in its table are never reached on this region. That is expected today (the kit plans an area) and is the documented ordering of decision 4; it will change with #4236, and the test comment says so.
- The `guide: Box::new(TracePlanner)` in the planner set is unused by the table (the kit refuses before the guide stage). Harmless; kept for the day #4236 lands.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

<!-- pr-reviewer: 33c116cfa93301d80cac41917153c522d560b90f -->

Needs changes before merge - one new interaction between the K2b helix family and the K4 order stage (the order stage refuses a valid helix guide set with a misleading reason; see the requested change).

Reviewed head 33c116cfa (DELTA: merge of side/path-kernel 7f70d8b1a / K4, PR #4234, into the K2b guide branch; remerge-diff ebc966350..33c116cfa, ~1700 lines). Trial merge against `origin/side/path-kernel` goes clean - no conflicts (the base has moved to df9ec30b6 since this merge: #4265 load control and #4253 link edge-band landed on it; `gh pr view` reports MERGEABLE / CLEAN). This is a DELTA review of the remerge-diff, not of the whole PR: the K2b core (medial/trace/helix planners) was reviewed at 2e7f78856 and ebc9663503.

What looks good

- The three hand-resolved conflicts keep both sides' behaviour, checked line by line:
  - `crates/geometry/src/geo2d.rs`: keep both sides' re-exports (`medial::{MEDIAL_MAX_SAMPLES, MEDIAL_REF, MedialAxis, MedialCurve}` and `segments::{point_segment_distance, segment_gap, segments_cross}`); `side_offset` kept. ✓
  - `crates/pathkernel/src/guide.rs`: `turn_of` keeps the K2b lead check (`same_lead` against `None` on both sides for non-helices) and returns `None` when the leads differ; `same_cut` is `turn_of(..).is_some()`, so the boolean law-3 semantics are unchanged. `same_lead(None, None)` is true, so the K4 order stage keeps its permutation check for every non-helical curve. ✓
  - `crates/pathkernel/tests/laws.rs`: the Gate map lists both sides' modules (`order::side/chain/stage`, `link::proof/route` added). ✓
- The merge-moved table test (`guide_trace::each_later_stage_refuses_the_chain_region_of_a_trace_by_name`) now covers K4's stages explicitly - `OrderStage` (`ORDER_NOT_PLANAR`) and `LinkStage` (`NOT_PLANAR_LINK` via `Hop::Lift`) - alongside the entry stage, the law kit's `planar`/`run`, and the kit only for the chain region of a trace. `catch_unwind` + named-reason assertions; no stage accepts the region. ✓
- The remerge-diff's other K2b-touching files (`guide/mark.rs` `follow`, `lib.rs` `to_loops`, `kit.rs` `Level::with_links`, `link_rule.rs`/`standins.rs` signatures) are coherent: marks follow their curve, `Level` carries the stay-down paths of the hops before it, and the note-keeping is unchanged.
- The K2b medial/delaunay/side-offset code keeps its own provenance headers (Blum 1967; Brandt and Algazi 1992; Attali and Montanvert 1996; Foskey/Lin/Manocha 2003; Ramer 1972/Douglas and Peucker 1973; Bowyer 1981/Watson 1981 with the Devillers visibility walk; Tiller and Hanson 1984 + Choi and Park 1999), its bounds (no `unwrap()`/`panic!()` outside tests; `locate` bounded at `2*triangles + 16`; `border` bounded; `fan` bounded), and its degenerate refusals (bad/non-finite tol, empty region, out-of-bounds samples, too-fine medial, path under 2 points, non-finite/zero offset). Provenance is clean-room, public literature, no vendor material. The `laws` suite pins the refusals and the law properties at the public API (146 pinned test fns, all green on the head).

Results merged with side/path-kernel (locally, worktree `.claude/worktrees/cc-pr4244-review`, PR head 33c116cfa, `RUSTC_WRAPPER=sccache`):

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test -p camcraft-pathkernel --test laws` | 146 passed, 0 failed (matches the body claim) |
| `cargo test -p camcraft-motion --test kernel_laws` | 29 passed, 0 failed |
| `cargo test -p camcraft-geometry --lib` | 99 passed, 0 failed (medial/delaunay/side_offset pins) |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-geometry -p camcraft-pathkernel -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean (0 warnings) |

The PR body's gate claim ("full batch, 1223 steps, 0 failed, 77.1 min") is not re-run locally here - it is a review of the remerge-diff, not a batch re-gate; the touched suites and clippy are green on the head. No example-catalog / post / toolpath suites are touched by the diff (the kernel stages are not wired into the app), so no example-catalog run. No heavy lane is reached; no P1 targeted heavy step. This PR is not P1 (the refusals are named, not wrong output).

Requested before merge

1. **The order stage cannot reverse a helix curve - and reports it with a misleading reason.** In the merged tree the K4 `order/stage.rs` `reversed()` rebuilds any curve with `Curve::new(...)`, which by K2b's construction refuses the whole helix family (`HELIX_NEEDS_LEAD`). Verified: a hole region (Inside), a `Circle(5,5;10)` helix choice with `Hand::Right`, run `OrderStage.order(set, r, &OrderChoice::default(), None)` - refused with `a helix curve needs its circle and its lead: make it with Curve::helix` (the curve has its circle and its lead; this read says nothing about the reversal that was asked of it). The the-helix test does not cover this: `guide_laws::the_helix_planner_holds_l1_to_l4` runs the kit's stand-in `SideOrder`, not `OrderStage`. The fix: rebuild the reversed helix through `Curve::helix` with the same `Lead` (the reversed sequence is valid under the same lead: same circle, same turns, same depth changes; `same_cut` and the permutation check still hold), or refuse with a named order-stage reason (for example `NOT_REVERSIBLE`); and pin the refusal/acceptance with one table test, the way the trace chain region test pins the later stages (`guide_trace::each_later_stage_refuses_the_chain_region_of_a_trace_by_name`).

Notes (not blocking)

- The base has moved: `origin/side/path-kernel` is now df9ec30b6 (K3 load control #4265, link edge-band #4253), not the 7f70d8b1a this PR merged against. The trial merge against the current base is clean and `gh pr view` says MERGEABLE. When the maintainer flags this ready to cut, the fresh base is fine - no refresh needed now.
- `docs/decisions/4177-kernel-order-link.md` is inherited from the K4 merge; the K2b decision record stays #4176, as the body describes. No process files changed (no `Process change: yes` needed).
- Cosmetic, not blocking: `crates/geometry/src/geo2d/segments.rs` doc paragraph repeats a sentence fragment ("A touch or a collinear overlap gives zero of one to the other segment (a touch or a collinear overlap gives zero that way)").

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

<!-- pr-reviewer: 6aa630feec8eebb98be69e4ed0f5e3fd7fc7e84d -->

Verdict: refresh required before merge. This is not a code finding. The helix fix at head 6aa630fe is verified clean. The base branch `side/path-kernel` has moved under the PR since the last refresh (df9ec30b6 to fd653b035, PR #4275, the Outside piece starts at the stock edge with a proved approach from the air). The trial merge with the current base has one conflict. The PR needs a re-merge with the base, a re-run of the touched suites, and a fresh review.

What looks good
- One rule for the class of the finding: a later stage restarts, reverses or replaces a curve through the constructor of that curve's family, or refuses by a reason of its own stage. In the order stage, a helix always runs down its lead. It is reversed only when the guide set holds it upward. A direction the hand does not give is named by the note `HELIX_HAND_SETS_DIRECTION`. A failed rebuild is `NOT_REVERSIBLE`. In the load stage, no pass is inserted before a curve that is not a ring (`NOT_A_RING`). Trochoidal loops leave a lead, an exact circle or a depth-changing curve as it is (`SHAPE_KEPT`). A refused rebuild is `SET_NOT_KEPT`.
- The pins pin the exact case. `later_stages::each_guide_family_keeps_its_data_or_is_refused_by_the_stage_in_each_later_stage` (7 rows, 13 stage cells) and `later_stages::the_order_stage_runs_a_helix_down_its_lead_and_names_a_direction_that_its_hand_does_not_give` (right and left hand, climb and conventional). Both are red with the old reversal (`HELIX_NEEDS_LEAD` from the Guide stage) and green with the fix. The table covers all three start sides (Auto, Inside, Outside).
- `same_cut` survives the reversal. The suite asserts it.

Results (base `side/path-kernel` at fd653b035; trial merge = this head merged with the base; the trial merge is local and never pushed)
- Trial merge: one doc-comment conflict in `crates/pathkernel/tests/laws.rs` (the gate map). I resolved it locally by keeping both sides. Everything else auto-merged (the base's #4275 changes). The merge commit is local: "trial merge (local review only)".
- `cargo test -p camcraft-pathkernel --test laws`: 163 passed, 0 failed (157 at the head alone, plus 6 from the base's `air_approach` module).
- `cargo test -p camcraft-motion --test pass_start_levels`: 44 passed (incl. `kernel_guides` x5: trace, slot centre, thread helix, circle rings, engrave).
- `cargo test -p camcraft-motion --test kernel_laws`: 30 passed, 0 failed. `k3_load::kernel_load_control_round_the_disc_and_the_dog_bone` (the known red of the base at this head alone, 337 and 77 against 334 and 74) is green on the trial merge, where the base's re-pin is used.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-geometry`: all suites green (medial, delaunay, side_offset).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-pathkernel -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-geometry --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Not run: the example catalog suites (no post or toolpath change; guide geometry only), the full heavy lanes (review does not run them; no P1 safety-floor work on the posted G-code), and the light lane. `cargo xtask gate light` did not finish in the 570 s box (release build not finished; exit 143). Reported as not run, not a pass. The full light lane runs at merge time.

Targeted tests
- The two new pins and the pathkernel laws suite: green.
- The K3 known red: green on the trial merge. The stale 337/77 at the head alone is a base state, not a finding in this PR.

Requested before merge
1. Merge the current `side/path-kernel` (fd653b035, PR #4275) into `issue/4176-kernel-guides-medial-trace-helix`. The only conflict is the doc-comment gate map in `crates/pathkernel/tests/laws.rs`; keep both sides. Then re-run the touched suites and re-flag the PR ready for a fresh review.

Notes (not blocking)
- The base moved after the PR was last refreshed (7922d0c6c, base df9ec30b6). The branch is not current.
- `docs/decisions/4176-kernel-guides-medial-trace-helix.md` records the fix well. `Changelog: none` is reasonable: no planner calls the new code yet.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
